text:
Sam W: Quick follow-up from the Triton vs CUTLASS RFC — we need a concrete prototyping plan to decide runtime selection criteria. TL;DR: land a small benchmark + fallback policy in 2 weeks. Thoughts?

Anya R: Agree. Proposal: 3 workloads (short-chat, long-chat, batching throughput). Run on A100-40GB and A10g. Measure latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and memory headroom. Do we include int8/4-bit quant variants?

Miguel P: Yes to workloads. Also measure KV-cache (load/unload) cost and peak workspace allocations. Triton currently wins small-batch low-latency; CUTLASS tends to win large matmuls / long contexts. Need numbers.

Jules K: Two integration questions: (1) how to represent kernel capability surface in our selector API, (2) fallback semantics — model correctness > perf, so fallback must preserve numerical compatibility or trigger model-safe rollback.

Priya S: I'll run quick perf scripts. Suggest ranking metrics: correctness (bitmatch ± tolerance), p95 latency, tail variance, token/sec, and memory fragmentation. Will add a CI harness to gate regressions.

Sam W: @Priya S awesome. Also we need an automated canary: if chosen kernel increases eval-error by >1% we auto-rollback. That ties into Redwood Optimize alerts.

Miguel P: Implementation idea: build a small 'kernel-probe' binary that can load model weights, run N warmup tokens, then run scenarios and emit a single JSON profile line. Example output:

```
{
  "model":"redwood-3b",
  "kernel":"triton_v2.1",
  "p95_ms":12.4,
  "tokens_per_sec":3200,
  "memory_peak_mb":21500,
  "compat_ok":true,
  "fallback_hint":"cutlass_v1.4"
}
```

This can feed the runtime selector and our perf dashboard.

Jules K: API sketch: runtime config keys `preferred_kernels: ["triton","cutlass"]`, `fallback_policy: "compatibility-first|perf-first|cost-first"`, `probe_profile_id`. Also add `kernel_tags` for quant/int8/ptx-level flags.

Anya R: Edge case: sparse or masked attention patterns. Need to ensure kernels advertise support for attention_masking / block-sparsity. Add an 'attention_masking' test in the probe scenarios.

InfraBot: Nightly perf job note: created nightly-compat-run in perf fleet (owner: @Priya S). ETA: 48h to start.

Priya S: Action items (drive):
1) Priya -> perf scripts + CI harness (due 2025-03-10)
2) Miguel -> kernel-probe binary + runtime hook (due 2025-03-17)
3) Jules -> selector API PR draft (due 2025-03-12)
4) Anya & Sam -> test plan + eval sets (due 2025-03-08)

I'll kick off baselines this afternoon on A100 and A10g, with int8 as second pass.

Sam W: Sounds good. Please add risks to the doc (memory fragmentation, quant mismatch, patch-level CUDA differences). We'll sync in the architecture meeting Friday. :thumbsup:

Anya R: noted, adding initial risk list now.

Miguel P: I'll prototype the probe CLI in a separate repo branch and push a PoC notebook with raw numbers.

Jules K: When we have probe output, we should wire rounded decisions into the rollout engine: canary -> small-percentage -> full. Keep manual override.

Sam W: Perfect. Thanks all.
